items.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I did have an aunt that lived across the street, my Aunt Minnie, a relative of – my father’s aunt. She was my great aunt.

ctx.x: Everybody was telling tales, like we used to call them, but they were bare­ faced lies. But we would call them tales, that we lived in the neighborhood, because I did have an aunt that lived across the street, my Aunt Minnie, a relative of – my father’s aunt. She was my great aunt. So I said, “Dad, I got to get into DuSable. I got to get in there.” He said, “You can’t get there, because you don’t live in that vicinity.” I said, “Dad, you got to work it out. Don’t you have somebody somewhere?” Sure enough, he had…
district, all of us that were in the band. Everybody wanted to be under Captain Walter Dyett, that great man that taught at DuSable. But that’s way down the line. I must have been 14 by that time.
